# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

Display the current status of all tasks

Usage: executable status [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...
          Users can specify a custom query to filter for specific values, order by a column
          or limit the amount of tasks listed.
          
          Syntax:
             [column_selection]? [filter]* [order_by]? [limit]?
          
          where:
            - column_selection := `columns=[column]([column],)*`
            - column := `id | status | command | label | path | enqueue_at | dependencies | start |
            end`
            - filter := `[filter_column] [filter_op] [filter_value]`
              (note: not all columns support all operators, see "Filter columns" below.)
            - filter_column := `status | command | label | start | end | enqueue_at`
            - filter_op := `= | != | < | > | %=`
              (`%=` means 'contains', as in the test value is a substring of the column value)
            - order_by := `order_by [column] [order_direction]`
            - order_direction := `asc | desc`
            - limit := `[limit_type]? [limit_count]`
            - limit_type := `first | last`
            - limit_count := a positive integer
          
          Filter columns:
            - `status` supports the operators `=`, `!=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `queued`, `stashed`, `paused`, `running`, `success`, `failed`
            - `command`, `label` support the operators `=`, `!=`, `%=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `some text`
            - `start`, `end`, `enqueue_at` contain a datetime
              which support the operators `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`
              against test values that are:
                - date like `YYYY-MM-DD`
                - time like `HH:mm:ss` or `HH:mm`
                - datetime like `YYYY-MM-DDHH:mm:ss`
                  (note there is currently no separator between the date and the time)
          
          Examples:
            - `status=running`
            - `command%=echo`
            - `label=mytask`
            - `columns=id,status,command status=running start > 2023-05-2112:03:17 order_by command
            first 5`
          
          The formal syntax is defined here:
          https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/state/query/syntax.pest
          
          More documentation is on the query syntax PR:
          https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/issues/350#issue-1359083118

def run_once(responder):
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(sock_path)
    s.listen(1)
    s.settimeout(6)
    result={}

        try:
            conn,addr=s.accept()
            conn.settimeout(4)
            # read secret
            hdr=conn.recv(8)
            print(f"HDR {hdr.hex()} len={struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0] if len(hdr)==8 else '?'}")
            n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
            sec=b""
            while len(sec)<n:
                sec+=conn.recv(n-len(sec))
            print(f"SECRET {sec!r}")
            # responder sends something
            resp=responder(conn, sec)
            # then try to read next message from client
            try:
                while True:
                    h=conn.recv(8)
                    if not h or len(h)<8:
                        print(f"next hdr short {h!r}")
                        break
                    print(f"NEXT HDR {h.hex()} -> {struct.unpack('>Q',h)[0]}")
                    nn=struct.unpack('>Q',h)[0]
                    payload=b""
                    while len(payload)<nn:
                        chunk=conn.recv(min(4096, nn-len(payload)))
                        if not chunk: break
                        payload+=chunk
                    print(f"NEXT PAYLOAD {len(payload)} bytes: {payload[:1000]!r}")
                    # try to read more? break after one
                    # keep listening for more?
                    conn.settimeout(1)
            except Exception as e:
                print("next recv exc",e)
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print("srv exc",e)
        finally:

# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

### Basic Commands

                     This means that the command needs proper shell escaping.
                     The safest way to preserve shell escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

def probe(args):
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(sock_path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(6)
    cap=[]
    def srv():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(4)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
            sec=b""
            while len(sec)<n: sec+=conn.recv(n-len(sec))
            v=b"4.0.4"; conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(v))+v)
            h=conn.recv(8); nn=struct.unpack('>Q',h)[0]
            pl=b""
            while len(pl)<nn: pl+=conn.recv(nn-len(pl))
            cap.append(pl)
            time.sleep(0.2); conn.close()
        except Exception as e: print(e)
        finally: s.close()
    import threading
    t=threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True); t.start(); time.sleep(0.2)
    # Use timeout 10, but client will fail after no response (early eof). That's fine.
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c",cfg]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=10)

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{args} => raw {cap[0][:300]!r} err {e}")
    else:
        print(f"{args} => no req")

    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(sock_path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(10)
    reqs=[]
    def srv():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(5)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
            sec=b""
            while len(sec)<n: sec+=conn.recv(n-len(sec))
            v=b"4.0.4"; conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(v))+v)

            h=conn.recv(8); nn=struct.unpack('>Q',h)[0]

            while len(pl)<nn: pl+=conn.recv(nn-len(pl))
            reqs.append(cbor_decode(pl))
            print(f"REQ1 {reqs[-1]}")
            enc=cbor_encode({"Status": first_state})

import subprocess, os, socket, threading, time, struct
fake="/tmp/fakehome2"; cfg="/tmp/test_pueue.yml"; sock_path=f"{fake}/.local/share/pueue/pueue_agent.socket"
env=os.environ.copy(); env["HOME"]=fake
def cbor_encode(obj):
    import struct as S
    if obj is None: return b'\xf6'
    elif isinstance(obj, bool): return b'\xf5' if obj else b'\xf4'
    elif isinstance(obj, int):
        if 0 <= obj <= 23: return bytes([obj])
        elif 0 <= obj <= 255: return b'\x18'+bytes([obj])
        elif 0 <= obj <= 65535: return S.pack('>BH', 0x19, obj)
        else: return S.pack('>BI', 0x1a, obj)
    elif isinstance(obj, str):
        b=obj.encode(); l=len(b)
        if l<=23: return bytes([0x60|l])+b
        elif l<=255: return b'\x78'+bytes([l])+b
        else: return S.pack('>BH',0x79,l)+b
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        l=len(obj)
        hdr=bytes([0xa0|l]) if l<=23 else b'\xb8'+bytes([l])
        return hdr+b"".join(cbor_encode(k)+cbor_encode(v) for k,v in obj.items())
    else: raise Exception("x")

def run_case(args):
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    import socket as S
    s=S.socket(S.AF_UNIX, S.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(sock_path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(8)
    def srv():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(5)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
            sec=b""
            while len(sec)<n: sec+=conn.recv(n-len(sec))
            v=b"4.0.4"; conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(v))+v)
            h=conn.recv(8); nn=struct.unpack('>Q',h)[0]
            pl=b""
            while len(pl)<nn: pl+=conn.recv(nn-len(pl))
            enc=cbor_encode({"Success": "hi"})
            conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(enc))+enc)
            conn.settimeout(2)
            try: conn.recv(8)
            except: pass
            time.sleep(0.1); conn.close()
        except: pass
        finally: s.close()
    import threading
    t=threading.Thread(target=srv, daemon=True); t.start(); time.sleep(0.2)
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c",cfg]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=10)
    print(f"ARGS {args} OUT {r.stdout!r} ERR {r.stderr!r} RC{r.returncode}")
    t.join(timeout=5)

run_case(["--color","never","clean"])
time.sleep(0.3)
run_case(["--color","always","clean"])
time.sleep(0.3)
run_case(["clean"])
PY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, time, struct, socket, json, datetime

VERSION = "4.0.4"

def prog_name():
    p = sys.argv[0] if len(sys.argv)>0 else "executable"
    b = os.path.basename(p)
    return b if b else "executable"

# CBOR encode/decode (minimal for pueue)
def cbor_encode(obj):
    if obj is None:
        return b'\xf6'
    elif isinstance(obj, bool):
        return b'\xf5' if obj else b'\xf4'
    elif isinstance(obj, int):
        if 0 <= obj <= 23:
            return bytes([obj])
        elif 0 <= obj <= 255:
            return b'\x18'+bytes([obj])
        elif 0 <= obj <= 65535:
            return struct.pack('>BH', 0x19, obj)
        elif 0 <= obj <= 4294967295:
            return struct.pack('>BI', 0x1a, obj)
        else:
            return struct.pack('>BQ', 0x1b, obj)
    elif isinstance(obj, str):
        b=obj.encode()
        l=len(b)
        if l<=23:
            return bytes([0x60|l])+b
        elif l<=255:
            return b'\x78'+bytes([l])+b
        elif l<=65535:
            return struct.pack('>BH',0x79,l)+b
        else:
            return struct.pack('>BI',0x7a,l)+b
    elif isinstance(obj, bytes):
        l=len(obj)
        if l<=23:
            return bytes([0x40|l])+obj
        elif l<=255:
            return b'\x58'+bytes([l])+obj
        else:
            return struct.pack('>BH',0x59,l)+obj
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        l=len(obj)
        if l<=23:
            hdr=bytes([0x80|l])
        elif l<=255:
            hdr=b'\x98'+bytes([l])
        else:
            hdr=struct.pack('>BH',0x99,l)
        return hdr+b''.join(cbor_encode(x) for x in obj)
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        l=len(obj)
        if l<=23:
            hdr=bytes([0xa0|l])
        elif l<=255:
            hdr=b'\xb8'+bytes([l])
        else:
            hdr=struct.pack('>BH',0xb9,l)
        body=b""
        for k,v in obj.items():
            body+=cbor_encode(k)+cbor_encode(v)
        return hdr+body
    elif isinstance(obj, float):
        return struct.pack('>Bd',0xfb,obj)
    else:
        raise Exception(f"cbor encode unknown {type(obj)}")

def cbor_decode(data):
    def dec(pos):
        if pos>=len(data):
            raise Exception("eof")
        b=data[pos]; pos+=1
        major=(b>>5)&0x7; info=b&0x1f
        def ru(info,pos):
            if info<24:
                return info,pos
            elif info==24:
                return data[pos],pos+1
            elif info==25:
                return struct.unpack('>H',data[pos:pos+2])[0],pos+2
            elif info==26:
                return struct.unpack('>I',data[pos:pos+4])[0],pos+4
            elif info==27:
                return struct.unpack('>Q',data[pos:pos+8])[0],pos+8
            else:
                raise Exception(f"ru {info}")
        if major==0:
            v,p=ru(info,pos); return v,p
        elif major==1:
            v,p=ru(info,pos); return -1-v,p
        elif major==2:
            l,p=ru(info,pos); return data[p:p+l],p+l
        elif major==3:
            l,p=ru(info,pos); return data[p:p+l].decode(),p+l
        elif major==4:
            l,p=ru(info,pos)
            arr=[]
            for _ in range(l):
                v,p=dec(p); arr.append(v)
            return arr,p
        elif major==5:
            l,p=ru(info,pos)
            m={}
            for _ in range(l):
                k,p=dec(p); v,p=dec(p); m[k]=v
            return m,p
        elif major==7:
            if info==20: return False,p
            if info==21: return True,p
            if info==22 or info==23: return None,p
            if info==26:
                return struct.unpack('>f',data[p:p+4])[0],p+4
            if info==27:
                return struct.unpack('>d',data[p:p+8])[0],p+8
            raise Exception(f"major7 {info}")
        else:
            raise Exception(f"major {major}")
    v,_=dec(0)
    return v

def parse_top(argv):
    # argv without prog name, e.g., sys.argv[1:]
    # Returns (verbose_count, color, config, profile, subcommand, sub_args, help_flag, version_flag)
    # Handles -v/--verbose, --color, -c/--config, -p/--profile, -h/--help, -V/--version
    # Exact error handling for duplicates, missing values, unknown, etc.
    verbose = 0
    color = "auto"
    color_set = False
    config = None
    config_set = False
    profile = None
    profile_set = False
    help_short = False
    help_long = False
    version_flag = False
    i = 0
    n = len(argv)
    # First, handle -- and subcommand separation? Top-level does not support -- before subcommand (as we saw: ["--","status"] gives error about subcommand exists, remove --). So -- is not supported at top? Actually ["--","status"] gave error "unexpected argument 'status' found, tip: subcommand 'status' exists...". Good. So -- at top is treated as end of options? But it still errors. Good. We'll handle -- as end of options for top? Actually for top, -- means no more options, rest are positionals (which should be subcommand?). But original treats `-- status` as unexpected argument 'status' with tip, not as subcommand. Good. So -- at top does NOT introduce subcommand, it just ends options and rest are unexpected positionals. Good.
    # Similarly, "-" as subcommand gives "unrecognized subcommand '-'".
    # We'll implement parsing accordingly.
    remaining = []
    while i < n:
        a = argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            # End of options: rest are positionals (should be subcommand? But original treats them as unexpected, not subcommand)
            # For top, after --, next arg is treated as unexpected argument, not subcommand (as we saw).
            # So collect rest as remaining positionals and break
            remaining.extend(argv[i+1:])
            # Mark that -- was seen? For error message, original says "tip: subcommand 'status' exists; to use it, remove the '--' before it" when remaining is a valid subcommand.
            # We'll handle after loop.
            i = n
            break
        elif a in ("-h",):
            help_short = True
            i += 1
        elif a in ("--help",):
            help_long = True
            i += 1
        elif a in ("-V", "--version"):
            version_flag = True

def get_data_dir():
    # For secret/socket: ~/.local/share/pueue/ (respect HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME)
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "/root")
    xdg = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME")

def do_handshake(sock, secret_bytes, is_json):
    # Send secret: 8-byte BE len + secret
    sock.sendall(struct.pack('>Q', len(secret_bytes)) + secret_bytes)
    # Receive version: 8-byte len + version bytes
    hdr = b""
    while len(hdr) < 8:
        chunk = sock.recv(8 - len(hdr))
        if not chunk:

            eprint("Error: \n")
            eprint(f"   0: {ansi('91', 'Failed to initialize client.')}\n")
            eprint(f"   1: {ansi('91', 'Daemon went away after sending secret. Did you use the correct secret?')}\n")
            eprint("\nLocation:\n")
            eprint(f"   {ansi('35','workspace/pueue_lib/src/network/client.rs')}:{ansi('35','99')}\n")
            eprint("\nBacktrace omitted. Run with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 environment variable to display it.\n")
            eprint("Run with RUST_BACKTRACE=full to include source snippets.\n")

def format_datetime_for_enqueue(delay_str):
    import re, datetime
    s = delay_str.strip()
    if re.fullmatch(r'\d+', s):
        secs = int(s)
        dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) + datetime.timedelta(seconds=secs)
        ms = dt.microsecond * 1000
        base = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
        return base + "." + str(ms).zfill(9) + "Z"
    m = re.fullmatch(r'(\d+)(s|m|h|d)', s)
    if m:
        num = int(m.group(1)); unit = m.group(2)
        mult = {"s":1,"m":60,"h":3600,"d":86400}[unit]
        secs = num*mult
        dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) + datetime.timedelta(seconds=secs)
        ms = dt.microsecond * 1000
        base = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
        return base + "." + str(ms).zfill(9) + "Z"
    dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    ms = dt.microsecond * 1000
    base = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    return base + "." + str(ms).zfill(9) + "Z"

    if sub == "add":

        envs = dict(os.environ)
        start_immediately = opts.get("immediate", False)
        stashed = opts.get("stashed", False)
        group = opts.get("group", "default")

        else:
            enqueue_at = None
        deps = opts.get("after", [])
        prio = opts.get("priority")
        label = opts.get("label")

        hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]

dt="2026-09-04T14:25:48.524854662Z"

    "enqueue_at": None, "start": None, "end": None,

}
def test(client, state):
    try: os.unlink(sock_path)
    except: pass
    s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(sock_path); s.listen(1); s.settimeout(8)
    def srv():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(5)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]

    def srv():
        try:
            conn,_=s.accept(); conn.settimeout(5)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]

import subprocess, os
def run_orig(*args):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
def run_clone(*args):
    # Use executable_test (copy of pueue.py) with same args, but need to handle basename difference in Usage (replace executable_test with executable for comparison)
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable_test"]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True)
    o=r.stdout.replace("executable_test","executable")
    e=r.stderr.replace("executable_test","executable")
    # For WARN/INFO timestamps, replace timestamp pattern HH:MM:SS with placeholder? Original and clone timestamps will differ by a second or so (since current time). For comparison, replace timestamps with XX:XX:XX?
    import re
    # Pattern for timestamp in logs: e.g., "14:43:57" with ANSI codes? Actually logs have "\x1b[2m14:43:57\x1b[0m" – replace timestamp inside ANSI?
    # Simplify: replace all occurrences of \d\d:\d\d:\d\d with HH:MM:SS
    o=re.sub(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d', 'HH:MM:SS', o)
    e=re.sub(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d', 'HH:MM:SS', e)
    ro=re.sub(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d', 'HH:MM:SS', r.stdout.replace("executable_test","executable"))
    # Actually need to do for both o/e from clone and orig? For orig, also replace timestamps.
    return o,e,r.returncode

def run_orig_norm(*args):
    import re
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+list(args), capture_output=True, text=True)
    o=re.sub(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d', 'HH:MM:SS', r.stdout)
    e=re.sub(r'\d\d:\d\d:\d\d', 'HH:MM:SS', r.stderr)
    return o,e,r.returncode

cases = [
    (["--help"], ["-h"]),
    (["--version"], ["-V"]),
    (["add","--help"], ["add","-h"]),
    (["status","--help"], ["status","-h"]),
    (["--unknown"], ["unknowncmd"]),
    (["add"], ["remove"], ["switch","1"], ["send","1"], ["completions"], ["completions","invalid"]),
]

        print(f"{args} match? {match} RC {c1}/{c2}")
        if not match:
            print(f"  ORIG OUT{o1[:200]!r} ERR{e1[:300]!r}")
            print(f"  CLONE OUT{o2[:200]!r} ERR{e2[:300]!r}")
PY"}

            hdr=conn.recv(8); n=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
